planting.note: Can go out as soon as the soil has warmed, since this variety's advantage is setting fruit earlier in cool conditions rather than any true frost hardiness.

directions: Severianin is a Siberian heirloom selected specifically for setting and ripening fruit reliably through short, cool growing seasons where nighttime temperatures routinely drop into the 40s during bloom. The compact, determinate plants need only light staking and funnel their energy into an early, concentrated crop of smooth, medium-sized red fruit with good old-fashioned tomato flavor. Its exceptional ability to hold pollen viability in chilly conditions made it valuable breeding stock for university tomato programs developing short-season, cool-climate slicers. Start seed indoors about 6 weeks before the last frost and transplant once soil has warmed, expecting an earlier first harvest than most standard tomato varieties.
